source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001] — I reviewed the BOM, and I really like the overall direction. It matches exactly what I was hoping for.

Before we proceed, I’d like your thoughts on a few items:

• Motors — I’m concerned that 200 RPM may be slightly too low to produce a strong, frothy matcha texture. Would increasing the RPM make sense while still preserving enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality, would a stainless steel or milk-frother-style head work better than the resin whisk?

• Spout — I want to continue with the solenoid solution. For both texture and the visual experience, the pour needs to be clean, controlled, and seamless through the full sequence (mix → open → pour).

• Splash / mess control — this is especially important for events. I want to ensure:
– little to no splashing while mixing
– a smooth, controlled stream from the spout without sputtering
– no drips after the valve closes
– effective seals that prevent anything from leaking into the base
– a splash guard or lip around the bowl if one is necessary

• Cleaning — if possible, the bowls and spout parts should either be removable or easy to clean.

I’m very happy with everything else. I’d like to hear what you think about these points and whether you would change anything before we finalize the BOM.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
That reasoning makes sense — I like having additional power while retaining control over the speed range.

I’m comfortable with 3000 RPM provided we are not operating at the maximum continuously. Being able to tune it for different levels of mixing, from a slow mix to higher-speed frothing, would actually be ideal.

With the increased RPM, I do want to ensure that:
• splashing remains controlled
• mixing stays smooth rather than becoming excessively aggressive at higher settings

If necessary, I’m open to installing a splash guard or fine-tuning the whisk position / bowl depth so the machine operates cleanly.

Overall, I approve of this direction.

source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001] — I reviewed the finalized BOM, and everything looks very solid. I’m really happy with the direction, and it seems like we are close to finalizing it.

Before moving ahead with the parts order, I want to verify a few last details:

• Motors — the listing refers to an eccentric output shaft. Can you confirm that the whisk will still rotate smoothly and concentrically, or would a straight/centered shaft provide better stability?

• Motor performance — I like having the flexibility of 3000 RPM, but I want to ensure we can tune the speed for smooth mixing without creating excessive splashing at the higher settings.

• Solenoid flow — because the valves are on/off, do you anticipate a smooth pour when they open, or could the initial release be too sudden? The goal is a clean, controlled pour without splashing.

• Power supply — when both motors, the solenoids, and the fans are operating under load, will we remain comfortably inside the capacity of the 12V 20A power supply?

• Splash control — given the higher RPM, can you confirm that the whisk location, bowl depth, and overall configuration will keep the operation clean? For events, I want the machine to be as splash-proof and mess-free as possible.

Everything else looks great. I just want these points fully resolved before the order is submitted.

Let me know what you think.

value_updates.shaft_rotation_criterion: Motor shaft and whisk coupling must support smooth, centered whisk rotation, using a straight or centered shaft if needed for stability.

The newest updates look excellent. Seeing the bowl integration, plumbing, drainage routing, and complete structure taking shape has made me even more enthusiastic about the project’s direction.

Looking ahead, I keep thinking about potentially using the Matcha Mixer in a retail setting if we decide to open a shop. With that possibility in mind, I’d like us to consider food-service and health department requirements early, while this is still a prototype.

As the build moves forward, I’d like to account for food-contact materials such as stainless steel, food-grade plastics, and food-grade silicone; ease of sanitation and cleaning; avoiding concealed spaces where liquid could accumulate or become trapped; simple removal of bowls, whisks, and other parts for cleaning; separation of liquids from electrical components; and maintenance/service access if anything eventually requires replacement.

When you have time, I’d also like details about the materials used wherever food makes contact, as well as any locations you believe may present cleaning or sanitation difficulties.

For the long term, it may be useful to retain documentation covering materials used, CAD files, the wiring layout, cleaning procedures, and exploded-view drawings if available. We don’t need all of this immediately, but the information could be extremely valuable if the project grows into something larger.

Everything looks fantastic overall, and I’m very eager to see the testing videos and final assembly. It’s incredible to watch this evolve from an idea into a working machine.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
On the motors, I believe your concern about speed is correct. I've chosen new motors rated for 1000RPM. The PWM controller will continue to provide adjustment from 0 through 1000 while retaining enough torque to mix the liquids.

The whisk is the difficult part because there aren't many choices that satisfy our requirements. We need a reasonably large mixing head so the entire bowl mixes properly. The bowl is approximately 9 inch in diameter, but the plastic mixing head included on the BOM measures only about 2.4" in diameter. By comparison, my original wire-whisk suggestion was approximately 4.5" in diameter. Although it is advertised for a 6qt bowl, I believe it could still perform well in our smaller bowl. A head resembling those used on handheld electric frothers/mixers would probably be ideal, but those are available only in very small sizes.

I don't expect splashing to present a problem. If the action becomes too aggressive, the motor speed can be adjusted while it is operating. As you proposed, we can also add a basic splash guard if splashing does occur.

For cleaning, the current design allows the bowl to be removed very easily. The custom spout will also be designed for removal so it can be cleaned without difficulty.

Overall, we are almost ready, and I'll update the motor to 1000rpm. For the whisk, perhaps we should select 2 different styles and test them to determine which performs best. The whisk should be among the simplest parts to replace with a new design if necessary, and a basic adapter should enable nearly any whisk to connect to our system.
